previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and a history of kidney transplant rejection was admitted for evaluation of a positive tuberculin skin test and a several-week history of non-productive cough. Chest imaging showed chronic interstitial changes without acute findings or cavitary lesions. Three sputum samples were collected, all with negative acid-fast bacilli smears, making active tuberculosis unlikely. The patient remained stable throughout the admission, with no fever, night sweats, or other systemic symptoms. Hemodialysis was performed as scheduled. He was discharged home with plans to follow up in the infectious disease clinic in two weeks to review pending sputum and blood culture results and determine if treatment for latent tuberculosis is needed. No medication changes were made during the hospitalization.
problems: Nonspecific reaction to tuberculin skin test without active tuberculosis
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with ESRD on HD, CAD s/p 2 DES in ___, hyperparathyroidism, 
anemia who presents with left-sided chest pain and nausea after 
a mechanical fall.
.
ACTIVE ISSUES:
.
# Fall: Patient's history was consistent with a mechanical fall, 
possibly related to peripheral neuropathy; there were nothing by 
history to suggest ACS or neurologic event preceding the fall. 
He was discharged with home phsical therapy
.
# Chest Pain: Patient's presentation was most consistent with a 
left lower rib contusion, with no fractures on imaging. ACS was 
deemed unlikely; EKG was unchanged and cardiac enzymes showed 
stable elevated troponin (likely secondary to renal disease) and 
non-elevated CK or CKMB. CXR was negative for pneumonia, 
pneumothorax, or mediastinal widening. Pain was controlled with 
acetaminophen.
.
# Nausea: The patient noted that he had experienced nausea 
before during dialysis. Pain may have also been contributing. He 
continued to experience intermittent nausea likely secondary to 
opiates used for pain control and perhaps his sevelamer. KUB was 
unremarkable and LFTs were within normal limits. His opiates 
were discontinued and once daily H2 blocker was started. His 
nausea improved.  
.
# Hallucinations: Unclear etiology. The patient reported visual 
hallucinations upon closing his eyes. He insisted he was not 
asleep, but this was in the differential. Regarding the visual 
hallucinations, he saw himself in different locations whenever 
closing his eyes. Opening his eyes would terminate the 
hallucination. Given his nausea, current dual antiplatelet 
therapy, and symptoms we obtained a repeat head CT that revealed 
small interval increase in the known bifrontal subdural fluid 
collections (likely chronic subdural hematomas or cystic 
hygromas). Neurosurgery was consulted and recommended no 
immediate intervention, but follow up in one month with repeat 
head imaging. Neurology was also consulted who believed the 
hallucinations were likely related to med effect and recommended 
discontinuing psychoactive medications. Multiple additional 
laboratory studies were sent to evaluate his peripheral 
neuropathy, many of which are still pending. He will be 
contacted for a follow up appointment.
.
# Subconjunctival hemorrhage: Secondary to trauma from fall. No 
evidence of orbital fracture or globe damage. Discharged with 
instructions to pursue Ophthalmology follow-up for full retinal 
exam.
.
# Hip and Foot pain: Resolved prior to discharge. The patient 
reported acute pain in his right hip and ankle. He was afebrile 
and without leukocytosis. His exam showed a bruise over the 
right hip with mild limited range of motion secondary to pain. 
No visible erythema or effusion. XRAY imaging revealed no 
fracture in the hip or foot. He was evaluated by Rheumatology 
who felt these pains were unlikely to be gout and more likely to 
be trochanteric bursitis of the hip or a soft tissue injury 
likely related to his fall. He will follow up with Rheumatology 
as an outpatient. 
.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Mr. ___,
.
You were hospitalized because you had rib pain and nausea during 
dialysis. An X-Ray of your ribs showed no fractures; it is 
likely that you bruised your ribs. The pain will improve over a 
few days. You may take tylenol (as instructed on the package) 
for this pain. Lab tests and an EKG showed that you were not 
having a heart attack.
.
The bruising around your eye was likely from your fall; the 
blood over the white part of your eye will resolve after a few 
weeks. You should see an Ophthalmologist to be sure that you 
have no further eye problems from the fall.
.
Your nausea was likely related to the dialysis, especially since 
you have experienced this before during dialysis. It was also 
worsened by pain medications. We stopped these and your nausea 
resolved. If you continue to experience nausea you may try 
taking Zantac 150 mg daily. We are including a prescription for 
this, but you may purchase it over the counter.
.
During your stay you experienced hip pain, which is likely from 
a bursitis (inflammation of a fluid sac). You were seen by 
Rheumatology and will need to follow up with them after 
discharge.
.
During your stay you also complained of visual hallucinations. 
We repeated the imaging of your head that showed chronic fluid 
collections that are a little bit larger. Neurosurgery saw you 
and felt you did not need surgery. Neurology also saw you and 
sent off some studies. They will contact you regarding a follow 
up appointment.
.
Please start taking Sevelamer 1600 mg (2 capsules) with snacks. 
Continue to take all of your other medications as previously 
prescribed.
.
Follow-up with your Nephrologist, your Rheumatologist, and an 
Ophthalmologist to evaluate your eye. You will need to schedule 
this appointment. You will also need to follow up with the 
Neurosurgeon for evaluation of your head in one month. You will 
need a repeat CT of your head at that time. Neurology will be 
contacting you for a follow up appointment.
